ground: O you who believe: when you rise for the prayer, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, wipe over your heads, and wash your feet up to the two ankle-bones. If you are in a state of major impurity (junub), purify yourselves fully. If you are ill or on a journey, or one of you comes from the low ground (having relieved himself), or you have touched women, and you find no water, then head for clean earth and wipe your faces and hands with some of it. God does not want to lay any constriction on you. He wants to purify you and to complete His blessing on you, so that you may be grateful.

triggers.how: syntax: 'rise toward', a motion with a goal
the goal of the rising
the fa- turns the rising into the first step of a sequence

findings.statement: 'When you rise for the prayer' names the moment of standing up, and the root's sense of resolving on something and setting out for it also lets the standing be heard as the start of a movement toward prayer, with the water on the limbs as its next steps.
findings.perceptible: The rite starts as a movement toward something, not as a list of chores: a person gets up, sets out, and on the way passes water over the body.

triggers.how: shared root, two ayat later: 'be ones who stand firm for God'
shared root: 'if you establish the prayer' in the covenant with Israel

findings.statement: The body rises for prayer here, and the same root asks two ayat later that the believers stand firm for God as witnesses to justice, so the ritual standing can be heard as the first form of an uprightness that goes on into justice.
findings.perceptible: Purification is a threshold: the person who stands up washed in 5:6 is the one asked to stand upright in justice toward enemies in 5:8.

triggers.how: the full-body wash is named with a different root

findings.statement: 'Wash' here is simply making water flow over a limb and carrying dirt away; in this ayah the full bath of the junub is called by another word (iṭṭahharū).
findings.perceptible: The Turkish reader's 'gusül' (full ritual bath) belongs, in this ayah, to the limb washing of ablution. The ayah keeps a plain word, flowing water on the skin, for the face and arms.

triggers.how: shared scene body.limbs
shared scene body.limbs
shared scene body.limbs
second limit marked by إلى

findings.statement: The ayah names four parts of the body and marks two of them with a limit (up to the elbows, up to the ankle-bones), so the washing follows a map of the body with its edges drawn in.
findings.perceptible: Spatial: the body is laid out from top to bottom (face, arms, head, feet), and bony landmarks mark where the water stops. The rite's measure lies in the anatomy itself.

triggers.how: the ayah closes by denying constriction, the opposite of rifq's ease
B001 gentleness and B004 the place one leans on are branches of the same word

findings.statement: The washing of the arm stops at the elbow. Its name comes from a root of gentleness and of 'that which eases a need' (mirfaq, a convenience), so the limit of the rite can be heard as already carrying the ease the ayah states at its end.
findings.perceptible: Relational: the word that marks the edge of the obligation belongs to the family of ease and support. The measure is drawn in a gentle place, and the closing 'no constriction' is foreshadowed inside the ruling.

triggers.how: contrast with the neighbouring verb: flowing water versus a passing hand
same verb for the earth-wipe

findings.statement: Besides 'pass the hand over and take away a trace', the wiping of the head can be heard as the light touch that does not rub hard, so the ayah alternates two gestures: water poured and flowing, and a hand passing lightly.
findings.perceptible: Bodily: the face and arms are drenched, the head is only brushed. Two textures of contact give the rite its rhythm.

triggers.how: the verb takes its object with بِ, while the washed limbs are direct objects

findings.statement: The heads are wiped 'with/over' (bi-) and not simply wiped, and this preposition has been heard as contact with the head, or with part of it, while the head is still the thing wiped.
findings.perceptible: The washed limbs are acted on directly; the head is only reached by a touch. The grammar reproduces the lightness of the gesture.

triggers.how: the genitive reading attaches the feet to the wiping phrase
the accusative reading attaches the feet to the washed limbs across the head

findings.statement: Read arjulakum, the feet join the washed face and hands; read arjulikum (also mutawātir), they sit next to the wiped head. Both readings keep the feet in the ablution and differ over which gesture reaches them.
findings.perceptible: Compositional: the feet stand at the seam between the two gestures, and the two readings show the ayah's order (wash, wash, wipe, feet) as a real joint in the text.

triggers.how: shared scene land.soil: the face of the earth
B011: camels 'wiping' the land, the traveller crossing ground
heading across ground toward the earth

findings.statement: The verb for wiping also names smooth bare level ground and the crossing of land on a journey. When the traveller finds no water and wipes with the earth's surface, the gesture can be heard in the same family as the ground they cross.
findings.perceptible: Material: for the traveller the medium of purification is the very ground under their feet. Hand, earth and journey belong to one root.

triggers.how: B005 links the name al-Masīḥ to 'wiping the afflicted'
B005 links the name to journeying in the land
the surah names al-Masīḥ repeatedly (5:17, 5:72, 5:75)

findings.statement: The wiping of head, face and hands shares its root with al-Masīḥ, the name this surah returns to again and again, which the lexicon connects with wiping the sick and journeying the land. Here the same ayah names the sick and the journey, while the wiping stays a plain ritual act.
findings.perceptible: Across the surah: the Turkish reader hears 'mesh' and 'Mesih' as unrelated. In Arabic the gesture every believer performs and the title the surah discusses come from one root.

triggers.how: shared root later in the surah (the offering reaching the Kaʿba)
shared root: God made the Kaʿba a standing (qiyām) for people, also sharing ق و م with قمتم

findings.statement: The ankle-bone is 'the bone that juts out'. The root's branches (a raised bone, a raised square house, a raised rank) form one concept of a hard prominence, so the lower limit of the washing shares its name with the Kaʿba the surah names later.
findings.perceptible: The Turkish reader knows 'Kâbe' only as a proper name. The same word describes the knob of bone at the foot, the point the body faces toward being named from the same shape of prominence.

triggers.how: B003 distancing and B001 side belong to the same word
explaining passage: 'nor junub, except passing through'
the remedy that ends the standing-apart

findings.statement: Junub names the state after intercourse, and the root heard with it (side, putting at a distance, the stranger) lets the junub be heard as one standing to the side, kept apart from the place of prayer until they wash.
findings.perceptible: Spatial: major impurity is a position, being at the side, at a distance, and the full wash brings the person back to the centre.

triggers.how: shared root: Form V, you purify yourselves (B003, by water)
same surah: those whose hearts God did not will to purify

findings.statement: The ayah uses the root twice: first the believers purify themselves (iṭṭahharū, by water), then God wants to purify them (yuṭahhirakum). The water rite stays a bodily act and is also heard as the place where God's purifying reaches them.
findings.perceptible: Causal and relational: the human washing and the divine purifying are two forms of one verb, and the second gives the first its purpose. The Turkish 'taharet' (hygiene) recovers its inner, moral side.

triggers.how: the fixed pair 'ill or on a journey' (2:184–185, 4:43)
elsewhere 'no constriction on the sick' (24:61, 48:17)

findings.statement: 'Ill or on a journey' is the Quran's recurring pair of people for whom a duty is eased, and here the pair opens the substitute of earth for water.
findings.perceptible: The reader hears the phrase that marks a concession, so the tayammum clause is recognised as an easing before its details arrive.

triggers.how: B002 includes the face shining
B001 uncovering

findings.statement: 'Journey' comes from a root of uncovering and of the face or dawn shining, so the traveller who wipes their face with earth is, faintly, in the family of an uncovered, brightened face.
findings.perceptible: A faint visual echo: a journey lays things bare, and the face that meets the earth is the face that 'dawns'.

triggers.how: 'came from': a return movement
B001 rising, B004 the earth's face: high against low
B003 cleaning oneself of filth

findings.statement: 'Comes from al-ghāʾiṭ' is the Quran's discreet way of naming relieving oneself, and the word's first meaning, a wide low sunken ground, lets the scene be heard as someone climbing back out of a hollow and then heading for the clean face of the earth.
findings.perceptible: Spatial: purification becomes a movement from low ground (ghāʾiṭ) to open, rising, clean ground (ṣaʿīd). The euphemism is a landscape.

triggers.how: the other conditions are addressed to 'you' (plural)

findings.statement: Illness, journey and touching are said of 'you' (plural), but coming from the low ground is said of 'one of you', a switch to the singular that keeps the private act at a distance.
findings.perceptible: The ayah's courtesy can be felt: the one bodily function it names is set on an unnamed individual.

triggers.how: Form III (mutual touching) against the variant Form I lamastum
the other party of the touching

findings.statement: Read lāmastum, the touching is mutual contact, the usual euphemism for intercourse; read lamastum (mutawātir), it can be heard as touching with the hand (B001). Both keep 'touching women' as a cause for renewing purity.
findings.perceptible: The two readings are the textual root of the juristic disagreement over whether ordinary touch breaks ablution. The Turkish reader sees why the schools differ.

triggers.how: the sick may have water they cannot use
the object not found

findings.statement: 'You find no water' is plainly not coming upon any, and the root's sense of means and capacity also lets it be heard as not being able to have water, which fits the sick person placed at the head of the list.
findings.perceptible: Causal: 'finding' is having access, so the clause covers both empty land and a body that cannot bear water.

triggers.how: B006 names the lustre (water) of the face
water poured on the face

findings.statement: The water missing here is plain water, and the root also names the 'water' of a face, its freshness and lustre, so washing the face can be heard as giving the face its water.
findings.perceptible: Material: the face that meets God is refreshed with the very substance the language uses for a face's bloom. Turkish 'yüz suyu' keeps a trace of this.

triggers.how: sister root (the lexicon gives تيممتك وتأممتك): pilgrims 'heading for' the House
the object aimed at
the rising toward prayer continues as a heading toward earth

findings.statement: Tayammamū, before it became the name of a rite, means 'aim for, head deliberately toward' (Ibn al-Sikkīt: 'make for good earth'), so the ruling can be heard as a movement of intent toward clean ground, as the pilgrims of 5:2 head for the House.
findings.perceptible: Motion and intent: the Turkish technical term 'teyemmüm' gets back its gesture of setting a course, and the substitute rite becomes a small pilgrimage to the ground.

triggers.how: water is exactly what is missing

findings.statement: The root that says 'head for the earth' also names al-yamm, the great water, so at the moment water fails the verb faintly carries the sea inside it.
findings.perceptible: A sound image: the substitute for water is named with a root that also means the sea, so absence and abundance meet in one word.

triggers.how: the only other form of the verb: 'do not aim at the bad (al-khabīth) to spend from it'
the good, against khabīth

findings.statement: In its three Quranic uses the verb aims either at the khabīth (forbidden in 2:267) or at the ṭayyib (commanded here), so heading for 'good earth' is also a choice of the good over the bad.
findings.perceptible: Aim carries a moral direction: tayammum is choosing what one reaches for.

triggers.how: the lexicons define ṣaʿīd as 'wajh al-arḍ', the face of the earth
B001 rising: Rāghib reports ṣaʿīd as the dust that rises
low ground against rising ground

findings.statement: Ṣaʿīd is the surface of the earth, which the lexicons call 'the face of the earth', so the traveller passes the earth's face over their own face. The root of rising lets the same earth be heard as ground that lifts, or dust that rises.
findings.perceptible: Face to face: the rite joins the human face to the earth's face. Coming from the low ghāʾiṭ, the person turns to what rises.

triggers.how: shared root: 'the good things are made lawful for you'
repeated
activates B003 istiṭāba, cleaning oneself of filth

findings.statement: Right after 'the good things are made lawful for you' in food, the earth used for purification is also called 'good', and after the ghāʾiṭ the root's sense of cleaning away filth (istiṭāba) can be heard too.
findings.perceptible: The same quality governs what enters the mouth and what touches the face: the ṭayyib runs from the table in 5:4–5 to the ground in 5:6.

triggers.how: wipe … with some of it
the parallel ayah lacks minhu

findings.statement: Unlike its twin in 4:43, this ayah adds 'from it', so the wiping can be heard as taking something of the earth onto face and hands.
findings.perceptible: Material: a trace of the earth actually passes to the skin.

triggers.how: B002 narrow place thick with trees
explaining passage: the constricted chest 'as if climbing into the sky' (yaṣṣaʿʿadu, same root as ṣaʿīd)
open level ground against a thicket

findings.statement: 'Constriction' is the plain sense, and the root's image of a dense tangle of trees, a narrow place one cannot get through, lets 'God does not want to set on you any ḥaraj' be heard as God not trapping the sick and the traveller in a thicket, because open earth is always within reach.
findings.perceptible: Spatial contrast: thicket against open ground. Where 6:125 pairs ḥaraj with a painful climb (yaṣṣaʿʿadu), here the ṣaʿīd lies flat underfoot.

triggers.how: 'God rules as He wills'
same surah: God did not will to purify their hearts

findings.statement: The surah opened with 'God rules what He wills', and here that will is named twice, once denied (constriction) and once affirmed (purifying and completing), while it stays God's will.
findings.perceptible: The sovereign will of 5:1 is revealed, at the level of the body, as a will to purify, which casts the rulings of 5:1–5 in the same light.

triggers.how: the same preposition returns with the blessing

findings.statement: Two things are said to be placed 'upon you': the constriction God does not lay, and the blessing He completes.
findings.perceptible: Compositional: the ayah weighs a burden against a blessing on the same shoulders and chooses the blessing.

triggers.how: 'I have completed My blessing upon you', three ayat earlier
the same object
the next ayah: remember God's blessing

findings.statement: The blessing declared complete in 5:3 is completed again here, over the washing body, so the religion's completion can be heard as reaching as far as water or a handful of earth on the face.
findings.perceptible: Scale: the great declaration of completion comes down to the most ordinary daily act, and 5:7 at once asks them to remember it.

triggers.how: the little that is enough: a handful of earth in place of water
B003 fullness of the udder, beside completion

findings.statement: 'That you may be grateful' is thanks for a blessing, and the root's image of the shakūr beast that fattens on scant fodder, or the plant that greens after the least rain, lets gratitude be heard as thriving on the little that has been made enough.
findings.perceptible: Bodily and material: the gratitude asked for is to flourish on a handful of dust as on water. Turkish 'şükür' gets back its image of growth.

triggers.how: softness and ease against narrowness
B005 livestock: the surah's first blessing is a herd

findings.statement: Niʿma is the blessing, and the root's softness and ease stand directly against the ḥaraj just denied. Its livestock branch recalls that the surah's first gift was the herd of 5:1.
findings.perceptible: Texture: narrow against soft. The blessing is felt as the opposite of constriction.

triggers.how: rising for the prayer (13 of 33 uses of qāma)

findings.statement: Ṣalāt here keeps its dominant Quranic role, the human worship practice (78 of 83 uses), and the whole ayah is the threshold to it.
findings.perceptible: Shows the ayah as a doorway: everything in it happens on the way to prayer.

triggers.how: the same address opens 5:1, 5:2, 5:8, 5:11

findings.statement: The address 'O you who believe' opens a new ruling in the series that runs from 5:1, tying the washing to the same covenant of believers.
findings.perceptible: Locates the ayah in the window's chain of commands under one covenant (5:7).

grammar: إِذَا قُمْتُمْ: a past-tense verb in a conditional, heard as 'when you rise / are about to rise' for prayer; the washing comes before the standing in prayer, not after it.
إِلَى ٱلْمَرَافِقِ / إِلَى ٱلْكَعْبَيْنِ: إلى marks a limit; whether the elbow and ankle themselves are washed is a known question the preposition leaves open.
بِرُءُوسِكُمْ: the washed limbs are direct objects, but the head takes بِ ('wipe over / with'), a lighter contact, read by some as reaching part of the head.
وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ: in the accusative the feet join the washed limbs even though the wiped head comes between them in the word order.
فَٱطَّهَّرُوا۟: Form V تطهّروا with the t assimilated into a doubled ṭ, a heavier form suited to the full-body wash; set against God's Form II لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ ('He purifies you').
أَوْ جَآءَ أَحَدٌۭ مِّنكُم: the plural 'you' switches to the singular 'one of you' for the bodily function.
لَٰمَسْتُمُ: Form III, the pattern of mutual action (touching one another).
مِّنْهُ: 'from it', i.e. some of the earth, absent from the parallel 4:43.
مَا يُرِيدُ … وَلَٰكِن يُرِيدُ: God's will stated first as a denial and then as an affirmation; مِنْ حَرَجٍ with مِن makes the denial total: not any constriction at all.
عَلَيْكُم … عَلَيْكُمْ: the same 'upon you' carries the constriction that is denied and the blessing that is completed.
variants: وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ (5:6:15; the data file lists it under 5:6:21) read وَأَرْجُلِكُمْ (mutawātir): the genitive attaches the feet to the wiping of the head rather than to the washing; both readings keep the feet in the ablution (F8).

لَٰمَسْتُمُ (5:6:35; the data file lists it under 5:6:44) read لَمَسْتُمُ (Form I, mutawātir): 'you touched' in place of 'you touched one another', opening plain bodily touch (ل م س B001) beside the euphemism for intercourse (B003) (F18).
reread: A person gets up and sets out for prayer, and on the way water passes over the body along a map with edges: the face, the arms as far as the elbow (named from a root of ease and support), a light touch on the head, and the feet down to the jutting ankle-bone that shares its name with the Kaʿba. The one who is junub stands to the side until a full washing brings them back. The sick, the traveller, the one climbing back from the low ground, the one who has touched: if water is out of reach they are not left in a thicket but head deliberately (tayammum) for the earth's own face, clean and rising, and pass it over their faces. The good (ṭayyib) that governed the table in 5:4–5 now governs the ground. Their washing (taṭahhur) is where God's purifying (taṭhīr) reaches them, and the blessing declared complete in 5:3 is completed down to a handful of dust. The gratitude asked for is that of the creature that flourishes on the little it is given.

set_aside.what: ص ل و B001 (meeting fire, roasting) and B004 (a snare set for game) on ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ
set_aside.why: Nothing in the ayah activates fire or a trap. The hunting snare could touch 5:4's hunt, but it has no member here and would cloud the plain word.

set_aside.what: غ س ل B003 (stallion that does not impregnate) and B004 (ghislīn, the fluid of hell)
set_aside.why: No trigger in the ayah or window. Ghislīn as an inverted washing belongs to ayat about the Fire.

set_aside.what: ر ء س B002 (leadership, heading a people) on بِرُءُوسِكُمْ
set_aside.why: The ayah's heads are only wiped; nothing activates rank. The Turkish 'reis' loss is noted, but the reading adds no payoff here.

set_aside.what: ر ج ل B002 (man, male) behind Turkish 'rical'
set_aside.why: The ayah's word is the foot. The male sense is only a Turkish false friend, handled under losses.

set_aside.what: ج ن ب B006 (south wind), B011 (shield at the side)
set_aside.why: No activation. The 'side' concept is kept via B001/B003/B004 in F12.

set_aside.what: م ر ض B002 (sickness of the heart)
set_aside.why: The surah has it (5:52), but here the sick are bodily, paired with the journey. Reading it in would push aside the plain concession rather than contain it.

set_aside.what: م س ح B003 (killing with the sword), B016 (smooth-talking deceit), B018 (crocodile)
set_aside.why: The war.battle and deceit scenes have no member in this ayah's action. They would contradict the gentle gesture without making anything perceptible.
The surah is full of 'the Book', but 'على سفر' here is a journey. The link is too weak to perceive in this ayah.

set_aside.what: ح ر ج B009 (the hunting dog's share of the game)
set_aside.why: 5:4's hounds (مكلبين) do make a faint trigger, but in 'no ḥaraj on you' the sense would be a pun without payoff.

set_aside.what: ح ر ج B006 (bier), B010 (ropes set for predators)
set_aside.why: The ropes could touch I1 (knots), and the bier the life.death scene, but neither is activated by the purification context. The thicket/narrowness reading carries the image.
Protective amulets are not in view. Completion (B001) and 'completing the shares' (B006, via 5:3) carry I3.

set_aside.what: ك و ن B004 (istikāna, submission) on كُنتُم
set_aside.why: The copula here only states conditions; no trigger lifts it.

set_aside.what: و ل ه (~alt root for ٱللَّه)
set_aside.why: Documented alternative with no activation in this ayah.

set_aside.what: ك ع ب B003 (a girl's breast rising) and B008 (virginity)
set_aside.why: 'Touching women' is present, but reading the ankle-bone this way adds nothing perceptible and would distract; the prominence concept (F11) is kept.

set_aside.what: و ج ه B002/B005 (face as direction, qibla)
set_aside.why: Real, but in this ayah the face is a surface to wash and wipe. The direction sense is carried by tayammum's heading (F21) and needs no separate finding.

loaded_words.role: the human worship practice, performed, kept, timed
loaded_words.departure: none; 'namaz' matches the role, but Turkish 'salât' has narrowed and loses the supplication and blessing sense (B002)

loaded_words.role: no dominant role; the largest group is rising for prayer or supplication
loaded_words.departure: translating it as 'intend to pray' (a common tafsir gloss) loses the physical rising that the ayah turns into motion

loaded_words.role: almost always negated: a constriction God does not lay (on the sick, the blind, the Prophet, in religion) or one felt in the chest
loaded_words.count: about 12 of 15 in the 'no ḥaraj on …' pattern
loaded_words.departure: Turkish 'zorluk/güçlük' gives difficulty and loses the narrow place and the thicket

loaded_words.role: bringing something to its full measure; with niʿma always God completing His blessing
loaded_words.departure: 'tamamlamak' fits; conversational Turkish 'tamam' ('okay') may weaken it

loaded_words.role: a benefit remembered, completed, thanked for or denied
loaded_words.count: no dominant role; 16 of 50 received or completed, 18 remembered or thanked
loaded_words.departure: Turkish 'nimet' drifts toward food and good things to eat, while here the blessing is purification and the completed religion

loaded_words.role: thanks in response to provision or help, often in 'la ʿallakum tashkurūn'
loaded_words.departure: 'şükür' keeps the role but loses B002, thriving on little

loaded_words.role: the good and lawful, set against al-khabīth
loaded_words.count: most of 16 uses in the ḥalāl/ṭayyib or khabīth/ṭayyib frame
loaded_words.departure: 'temiz' (clean) for ṣaʿīd ṭayyib keeps purity but loses 'good, lawful, pleasant' and the link to 5:4–5

loaded_words.role: aiming at, choosing (the khabīth forbidden in 2:267; good earth here)
loaded_words.departure: Turkish 'teyemmüm' names a technique and loses the act of heading toward

loaded_words.role: an agent (God, a prophet, alms) purifying a person, a house or a heart
loaded_words.departure: 'taharet' is heard as hygiene; the Quranic role is a transforming purification that God performs

loaded_words.role: no dominant role; one group is having or lacking practical means
loaded_words.departure: 'bulamazsanız' keeps finding but loses 'lacking the means to use'

loaded_words.role: a messenger, sign or truth arriving
loaded_words.departure: here outside the dominant role: a person arriving from a place (the ghāʾiṭ), in the physical-arrival group

losses.loses: The ayah never names a rite: it lists acts on limbs (wash, wipe) and limits. 'Abdest' (Persian, 'hand-water') packages them into one technical term.
losses.adds: A settled ritual frame and school details the ayah does not state

losses.loses: In Arabic ghasl is any washing; in this ayah it is the limb washing, and the full bath is iṭṭahharū.
losses.adds: Turkish 'gusül' makes the reader expect a full-body wash where the verb is used for face and arms

losses.loses: The root's family: flat bare ground, crossing land, and al-Masīḥ (B005, B009, B011).
losses.adds: A narrow technical sense (wet hand over head or khuff)

losses.loses: Being at the side, set apart (B001, B003); the state is a position of distance from the place of prayer.
losses.adds: 'Cenabet' carries a slang sense of vile or filthy that the Arabic state lacks

losses.loses: Moral and inner purification (B005), and God as the one who purifies.
Aiming, heading deliberately for (B001); kinship with 'āmmīn' (5:2).
losses.adds: A fixed technique detached from movement

losses.loses: 'The face of the earth' (wajh al-arḍ) and the root of rising; ṭayyib's range of good, lawful and pleasant.
losses.adds: 'Toprak' (soil) narrows it to dirt, whereas ṣaʿīd is the earth's surface whether dusty or not (a known lexical dispute)

losses.loses: The narrow place and dense thicket (B001, B002), the spatial picture of being hemmed in.
Uncovering and the brightening face (B001, B002); the traveller as the one crossing distance.
losses.adds: Military campaign, a scheduled trip, a guest

losses.loses: Little here; the bodily sense matches.
Nothing; Turkish keeps the image of the face's 'water' as honour and lustre.
losses.adds: Turkish 'yüz suyu' leans toward honour; the Arabic B006 is freshness and bloom

losses.loses: 'Topuk' (heel) is not the jutting ankle-bone; the link to the Kaʿba's name (prominence) is invisible.
losses.adds: Turkish 'Kâbe' is only a proper noun

losses.loses: The elbow's kinship with gentleness, support and ease (rifq, mirfaq).
losses.adds: 'Refakat' is escorting, unrelated in the reader's ear
